title: When does a diagonal cut a corner into two equal angles?
description: A diagonal is drawn in a rectangle whose sides differ, and then in one whose two sides at the corner are equal, and the two angles at the corner are compared. Keeko's doubt is that a square is not a rectangle, and the video breaks it.
teaching_notes: One idea: a diagonal cuts a corner of a rectangle into two equal angles only when the two sides at that corner are equal, which makes the rectangle a square. Watch for students who think a square is not a rectangle.

source: How should the rectangle be constructed so that the diagonal
video_script.why: A learner compares the two angles a diagonal makes at a corner, first for a rectangle with different sides and then for one with equal sides, and sees when they are equal.
video_script.substitution: the book's rectangle PQRS with the diagonal PR, once with different sides and once with the two sides at the corner five centimetres each
video_script.anchor: the rectangle PQRS of the book with the diagonal PR cutting the corner at P
video_script.wrong_answer: a square is not a rectangle
video_script.wrong_move: believes the sides at a corner can never be equal in a rectangle, because a square is a different shape
video_script.payoff_line: The two sides at the corner must be equal, so the rectangle must be a square.

final_answer.value: a square; each corner is cut into 45 degrees and 45 degrees
final_answer.spoken: the rectangle must be a square, and each corner is cut into forty five degrees and forty five degrees

maths_rules: each corner of a rectangle is a right angle, 90 degrees
when the two sides at the corner are equal, the diagonal cuts the corner into two equal angles
a square has four right angles and equal opposite sides, so a square is a rectangle
video_script.design: The rectangle PQRS and its diagonal PR stay on the board. The sides are first different, then made equal, and the two angles at P are measured each time.

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book about the rectangle pee queue are ess.
<bookmark mark='cut'/>A line from pee to are cuts the corner at pee into two smaller angles.
How should the rectangle be made so that these angles are equal?

beats.on_screen: the question stays on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: the line PR glows and is labelled diagonal; the corner at P shows two smaller angles

marks.diag: the line from P to R glows and is labelled diagonal
marks.cut: the right angle at P is shown cut into two smaller angles

narration: <bookmark mark='diag'/>A line joining two opposite corners of a rectangle is called a diagonal.
<bookmark mark='cut'/>The diagonal pee are cuts the right angle at pee into two smaller angles.

beats.on_screen: Given: rectangle PQRS, diagonal PR cutting the corner at P
narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, a rectangle pee queue are ess, with the diagonal pee are cutting the corner at pee.

beats.on_screen: To find: how the rectangle must be made so that the two angles at P are equal

marks.find: the question is written under the given line

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find how the rectangle must be made so that the two angles are equal.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: draw a rectangle with different sides and join P to R; the two angles at P are not equal

marks.unequal: a rectangle with a long side and a short side is drawn with the diagonal PR
marks.see: the two angles at P are shown unequal, the one next to the long side smaller

narration: <bookmark mark='unequal'/>Step one, draw a rectangle with sides that are different, and join pee to are.
<bookmark mark='see'/>The diagonal leans towards the longer side, so the two angles are not equal.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: make the two sides at the corner equal, 5 cm each, and join P to R again

marks.equal: the sides at P are redrawn equal, 5 cm each, with equal-side ticks

narration: <bookmark mark='equal'/>Step two, make the two sides at the corner equal, five centimetres each.
<bookmark mark='again'/>Then join pee to are again.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: measure with a protractor: 45 degrees and 45 degrees; 45 + 45 = 90 degrees, the whole corner

marks.measure: the protractor reads 45 degrees for each angle at P
marks.sum: the two angles are added and fill the right angle

narration: <bookmark mark='measure'/>Step three, measure both angles with a protractor. Each one is forty five degrees.
<bookmark mark='sum'/>Forty five and forty five make ninety degrees, the whole corner.

beats.on_screen: Answer: a square; each corner is cut into 45 degrees and 45 degrees

marks.res: the square is shown with 45 degrees marked on both sides of the diagonal

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The two sides at the corner must be equal, so the rectangle must be a square.
<bookmark mark='res'/>Then the diagonal cuts each corner into forty five degrees and forty five degrees.

narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

marks.fix: the four right angles and the equal opposite sides are marked on the square

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks a square is not a rectangle, so the sides cannot be equal.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>But a square has four right angles, and its opposite sides are equal as well.
<bookmark mark='keep'/>A square is a special rectangle, whose sides at a corner are equal.
